chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
There is no man who grants security to a man upon a covenant of protection, then kills him, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing a banner of treachery.

key_terms.ذِمَّة: Covenant of protection; a formal pledge of security granted to a non-combatant or enemy; in Islamic law, the dhimma establishes mutual obligations of protection
key_terms.لِوَاء الغَدْر: Banner of treachery; a symbolic marker of shame carried on the Day of Resurrection by those who violated trust

ai.seo_question: What happens to someone who breaks a pledge of security in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues a severe warning against breaking a pledge of security (dhimma): the one who grants protection to another and then betrays and kills him will be publicly marked on the Day of Judgment with a banner of treachery. This hadith addresses a practice relevant to warfare and relations with non-Muslims, where granting aman (safe-conduct) was a solemn contract. The visible banner of betrayal in the afterlife reflects the Islamic principle that violations of trust carry permanent moral stigma.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Yahya Bin Imran, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘There is none from a man who grants security to a man upon a responsibility, then kills him, except that he would come on the Day of Judgement bearing a banner of the treachery’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Yahya ibn ‘Imran from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Whoever provides a commitment of immunity to someone but then kills him, he on the Day of Judgment will come, carrying the banner of betrayal.’”
